review: The repeated third line is the hymn's whole device: each stanza ends with the same interrogative frame (وَمَا أَنَا … مِنْ أَجْلِك), and the Hebrew keeps it word-for-word except for the one verb, so the stanzas are judged against each other.

1:1–2 הֲרֵיקוֹתָ … וַתָּגָר — the Arabic أَخْلَيْتَ نَفْسَكَ … وَجُلْتَ فِي الدُّنْيَا is Phil 2:7's emptying followed by a sojourn; הֵרִיק is the glossary verb for ἐκένωσεν, and גּוּר is kept for the alien stay (Gen 12:10, וַיָּגָר), so the world is a place He lodged in, not merely visited.
2:2 בַּלָּהָה — Job 24:17 and Ps 88:16 (אֵימִים), the biblical terror-noun, chosen for الْهَوْل so the escape is from dread and not from a vague 'danger'.
3:1 טָעַמְתָּ … מְרִירוּת — the Arabic ذُقْتَ … مَرَارَةَ الْعَذَاب keeps the taste metaphor, and the Hebrew keeps it with טָעַם (Ps 34:9, טַעֲמוּ וּרְאוּ) rather than a flat 'you suffered'.

4:1 הַסְּלִיחָה — the noun is post-biblical in this absolute form (the biblical verb is סָלַח); it is accepted here because the Arabic الْغُفْرَانِ is likewise a noun, and the verbal noun keeps the line's balance with הַתְּשׁוּעָה.
